To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=0,$ we plug $a=0$ into the general formula to give

$$
{P}_{2}(x)=f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)(x-0)+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(0)(x-0)^{2}.
$$

So, we need to work out $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ and ${f}^{″}(0):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1+2x) & ⟹ &  & f(0) & =\frac{\pi }{4} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{2}{1+(1+2x)^{2}} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(0) & =1 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\frac{8(1+2x)}{(1+(1+2x)^{2})^{2}} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(0) & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

We now plug the results for $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ and ${f}^{″}(0)$ into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =\frac{\pi }{4}+x+\frac{(-2)}{2}{x}^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}+1\,x-1\,{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
